findings.title: Advisory lock only covers dopemux auth writers
findings.body: src/dopemux/auth/hashfile.py exclusive_lock docstring and write_hashes/write_meta: writers must call exclusive_lock; write_hashes/write_meta do not self-lock. Hand edit of memory-token-hashes.json bypasses mutual exclusion (disclosed). A concurrent non-CLI writer or manual edit can still race with CLI apply paths. OPERATOR: decision pending.

findings.title: Missing filelock yields ImportError not HashFileError
findings.body: hashfile.py exclusive_lock: from filelock import FileLock, Timeout inside the CM; auth_commands apply paths catch (AuthError, OSError) only. Fail-closed (no unlocked apply) but operator message is a traceback rather than the HashFileError path. OPERATOR: decision pending.

findings.title: Missing `filelock` package raises uncaught `ModuleNotFoundError` instead of `HashFileError` / `ClickException`
findings.body: [src/dopemux/auth/hashfile.py:79] In `exclusive_lock()` (`src/dopemux/auth/hashfile.py:79`), `from filelock import FileLock, Timeout` is executed lazily inside the context manager, while `src/dopemux/commands/auth_commands.py:117,155,185` catches only `(AuthError, OSError)`. If `filelock` is missing from the runtime environment, `--apply` fails closed before generating a token or modifying state, but exits with an unhandled `ModuleNotFoundError` traceback rather than converting it to `HashFileError` / `click.ClickException`. Corroborating auditor. OPERATOR: decision pending.

findings.title: Mid-`rotate` failure after keychain overwrite leaves keychain and hash file out of sync until retry
findings.body: [src/dopemux/commands/auth_commands.py:145] In `rotate` (`src/dopemux/commands/auth_commands.py:145-148`), `store_token(principal, token)` overwrites the keychain item (`add-generic-password -U`) before `hashfile.write_hashes(kept)` updates `memory-token-hashes.json`. If `store_token`'s read-back or `write_hashes` fails after the keychain item was updated, the keychain holds the new token while the hash file retains the old hash. This is not worse than before this change, fails closed for the new token, and is recoverable by re-running `dopemux auth rotate <principal> --apply`. Corroborating auditor. OPERATOR: decision pending.

findings.title: Stale `$` anchor in error message text and one test-file helper regex, plus two E501 lines in test file
findings.body: [src/dopemux/memory/capture_client.py:78] `src/dopemux/memory/capture_client.py:78` still formats `^internal:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$` in its `CaptureError` message string after `_INTERNAL_PRINCIPAL_RE` at line 64 was updated to `\Z`; `tests/unit/runner_memory_2a_r2_w06/test_local_writer_principals.py:28` still uses `$` in its test-only `PRINCIPAL_RE`; and `tests/unit/runner_memory_2a_r2_w03/test_auth_helper.py:181,195` exceed 88 columns (109 and 89 chars). Corroborating auditor. OPERATOR: decision pending.

findings.title: Server hash-file refresh stamp uses `(st_mtime_ns, st_size)` without `st_ino`
findings.body: [docker/mcp-servers-source/conport/auth_identity.py:225] In both `docker/mcp-servers-source/conport/auth_identity.py:225` and `services/working-memory-assistant/auth_identity.py:184`, `AuthGate._refresh()` detects file changes via `(stat.st_mtime_ns, stat.st_size)`. Because `rotate` replaces one 64-character hex SHA-256 digest with another for the same principal, `st_size` is unchanged across a rotation, relying entirely on `st_mtime_ns` advancing. Including `stat.st_ino` (since `_write_json_atomic` always replaces the file with a new inode) would harden change detection on coarse-timestamp mounts. Corroborating auditor. OPERATOR: decision pending.
